A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CausalVLBench study. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite section relocation and table renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and Appendix D report original LVLM evaluations, prompting comparisons and counterfactual analyses on Pendulum, Water Flow and Causal Circuit.

after.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 retain the original empirical evaluations, while Appendix C adds precision/recall and graph-structure diagnostics.

M1.justification: The task formulations, construction of predicted graphs from Yes/No answers, prompt templates and two-stage chain-of-thought procedure are retained. The added diagnostics analyze model outputs without changing the benchmark procedure or evaluated architectures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three datasets and the same causal-structure, intervention-target and counterfactual tasks. The new diagnostics and examples use existing coverage; newly cited benchmarks are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same nine LVLM variants and comparison subsets. DeepSeek-VL2-Small labels are standardized to 16B, matching the configuration already described in v1, without evidence of a replacement model.

E3.justification: v2 adds precision/recall evaluation for zero-shot standard and interleaved structure inference, plus bidirectionality and cyclicity metrics for standard inference (Tables 9–10). The existing splits, 1,000 sampled queries per run, shot settings and primary metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds focused analyses of Yes/No response bias and predicted-graph directionality versus cyclicity. Figure 10 adds three illustrative Gemini reasoning traces. Existing graph-removal, demonstration-selection, chain-of-thought and counterfactual breakdown analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and a single Gemini evaluation because of rate limits. The new tables extend the existing subscript uncertainty-reporting format without introducing different run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing result values in Tables 1–7, the matched per-variable tables and Figure 3 are unchanged. New Tables 9–10 report additional diagnostics: for example, IDEFICS2 has Causal Circuit recall of 1.5% for standard and 0.9% for interleaved inference. Figure 10 adds qualitative model outputs.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces formal definitions of normalized bidirectionality and matrix-exponential cyclicity in Equations 7–8, together with a three-node cycle example distinguishing unidirectionality from acyclicity. Existing SCM, task and data-generation mathematics remain unchanged; no new proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and principal claims about limitations of visual causal reasoning and few-shot learning. The added concluding recommendation about causal reasoning in training reiterates motivation already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets precision/recall patterns as Yes/No response biases and associates bidirectional and cyclic predictions with failure to distinguish directionality from acyclicity. Existing explanations and limitations concerning four-variable systems and restricted proprietary-model coverage are retained.

D1.justification: Model configurations in Table 8, hardware, data-generation and sampling instructions, prompt procedures and code/data access information are retained. Standardized DeepSeek labels reconcile information already supplied in v1 rather than documenting a new configuration.

R1.justification: The benchmark discussion adds Wang (2024), Miliani et al. (2025) and Li et al. (2025a), refining comparisons with text and high-level multimodal causality benchmarks. Zheng et al. (2018) is newly cited for the cyclicity metric. Most existing positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A to main-text Section 2, and the remaining appendices are relabeled. v2 adds Ethical Considerations and makes limited results/conclusion edits and model-name corrections. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds diagnostic Tables 9–10 and reasoning-example Figure 10. The original per-variable Tables 9–11 become Tables 11–13 on a separate page, and Figures 8–9 are resized and repositioned. Existing task diagrams and counterfactual plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 9–10 make response biases and graph inconsistencies more visible, while Figure 10 and the expanded related work improve transparency and context. These are useful, focused gains. However, correlated bidirectionality and cyclicity scores alone do not establish the new claim that models cannot distinguish those concepts, limiting the strength of the added interpretation.
